name: 哈罗德
src: 月银纪史诗/第七歌_焚原断刃.md:1190
who: Harold, the human lord of a river city built on two forks of the grain river and crossed by two arched stone bridges, a little past fifty, who keeps the south gatehouse and nails up bounties he cannot pay in gold: about 180 cm, broad-chested and heavy-shouldered, a former spearman whose hands have grown slow. Faded copper-red hair cropped short and gone half grey, a close-clipped beard of the same, deep-set river-green eyes with heavy crow's feet, a broad nose once broken. Thick, scarred spearman's hands. He cannot read, yet knows every name on his lists by heart. One twisted bronze arm ring on his left forearm (on the viewer's right when he faces us). A gruff, plain-spoken, stubborn air, his grief kept behind a habit of counting who is missing.
face: FACE, as in the references: a weathered man of about fifty-two, deep-set river-green eyes with heavy crow's feet and a furrow between the brows, a broad nose with an old break, lined cheeks, short copper-red hair and a close-clipped beard both half gone grey. Skin shadows a warm tone.
build: 180 cm, broad and heavy: a deep chest, thick shoulders and arms, a little thickened at the middle with age.
palette: river slate blue, faded copper red, bronze, oiled brown leather, oat straw
casual: The lord at his gatehouse: a knee-length straight-cut wool over-robe dyed slate river-blue, fastened at the collar with a bronze clasp cast as two small arched bridges, a wide leather belt with a heavy iron key ring, dark wool trousers and laced boots; the twisted bronze arm ring on his left forearm (on the viewer's right when he faces us). He holds a worn leather horse halter with a brass ring in one hand, the halter of a horse that came back without its rider. Standing square, a gruff, tired look.
private: In the stable before dawn: the robe off, a long-sleeved undyed wool tunic belted with a cord, the sleeves pushed up, plain trousers, old boots with straw stuck to them; he holds a wooden bucket of oats against his hip and a wooden scoop in the other hand. A quiet, inward look.
battle: Taking his old spear down in the gatehouse door, in the bridge-lords' handed-down war gear, a little tight on him now: a boiled-leather cuirass and shoulder guards stitched with overlapping bronze scales, each scale stamped with the twin-arch bridge sign and holding a faint core-light at its rim; a short slate-blue over-robe belted over it; leather bracers, the twisted bronze arm ring glowing faintly; a round linden shield painted with two white arches on his left arm. In his right hand the long family spear, its old leaf-shaped head carrying a thin line of pale river-blue light along both edges, levelled low. Planted in a narrow stance as if blocking a bridge, the jaw set.
formal: Reading out the names before a sortie: a fresh slate-blue wool over-robe to the shin, a broad bronze collar clasp of twin arches, a dark blue cloak pinned at one shoulder, a thin bronze circlet, the arm ring polished, clean boots. No paper in his hands; the hands are clasped behind his back and the head lifted, as if reciting by heart.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait in a stable doorway at grey dawn, warm lantern light from one side and cold blue morning from the other; he looks off to the side, gruff and tired, holding out a scoop of oats. Foreground blur: drifting hay and the edge of an empty saddle.
gear: 灵格｜富（守桥领主家，眼下城里钱紧）｜照常｜3档｜灵格本是二档，几代守桥的领主家加一档，穿家传的成套甲，招牌是那杆挂在门楼墙上的守桥长枪；手慢了，甲也有点紧。

name: 达格妮
src: 月银纪史诗/第七歌_焚原断刃.md:1269
who: Dagny, a dwarf woman, master smith of the First Furnace in the forge-heart under the mountain, about a hundred and eighty years old and looking a dwarf woman's forty: about 136 cm, small, stocky and broad-shouldered, forearms thick from the hammer. Dark wine-red hair wound in one thick braid around her head, a few ends singed. Pale flame-blue eyes, narrowed as if always reading the colour of a fire. A pale old burn scar across the back of her right hand (on the viewer's left when she faces us). No beard. She has never left the mountain and never fights; every failed ingot she makes is carved with its number. Terse and stubborn, and oddly afraid of heat: she always stands half a step back from the fire.
face: FACE, as in the references: a grown dwarf woman's face of about forty, NOT a child: a broad face, a strong straight nose, pale flame-blue narrowed eyes with fine lines at the corners, a smudge of soot on one cheekbone, a firm unsmiling mouth. Skin shadows a warm pink-orange.
build: 136 cm, small and stocky: broad strong shoulders and thick forearms, a B-cup, a solid waist.
palette: furnace orange and ember red, dark wine red, soot black, scorched leather brown, a little flame blue
casual: At the First Furnace: a heavy leather apron pocked with spark holes over a coarse forge-city linen shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, short wool trousers, iron-toed boots, a wide belt with a pouch of chalk and a small scribing chisel. A small hammer in her right hand and long iron tongs in her left, the tongs held a little away from her as if from heat. A flat, measuring look.
private: Resting by the scrap shelves after a failed trial: the apron off, a long-sleeved brown wool tunic belted with a cord, trousers, felt slippers, the braid loose over one shoulder; she holds a small horn cup of dark ale in one hand and a cracked ingot carved with a number in the other, turning it in her fingers. Tired, still counting.
battle: At the mouth of the furnace for the next trial, in the best forge kit of the forge-heart: a full-length apron of fire-mane wolf hide scraped smooth, faint sparks running along its seams; long rune-struck iron-backed gauntlets to the elbow, the runes glowing ember red; a rune-iron face shield pushed up on her brow; iron-toed boots. The long tongs grip a glowing ingot held out at arm's length, and the small hammer is raised in her right hand, a thin line of white-blue fire along its face. She leans half a step back from the heat, the eyes narrowed.
battle_pose: 3) the forge outfit: at work, not fighting, leaning half a step back from the heat, the long tongs held out at arm's length with a glowing ingot, the small hammer raised in the other hand, the eyes narrowed.
formal: On a forge feast day: a clean dark wine-red wool dress to the ankle with a broad tooled leather belt, a short soot-black wool cape pinned with an iron brooch cast as an anvil, the braid freshly wound and held with an iron pin, polished boots. She stands straight with the hands folded, a reluctant, faintly embarrassed look.
art: A portrait lit from below by white-blue furnace light, the face half turned and leaning a little away from the glare, the eyes narrowed, reading the colour of the fire; cool stone shadow on the other side. Foreground blur: drifting sparks and the edge of a stone shelf of numbered failed ingots.
gear: 极境｜中（第一炉的锻师）｜不打仗｜3档（锻炉装）｜极境本该三档，她一辈子不打仗，第三格画她试炉那一身：焰鬃狼皮整幅围裙、带符文的长护手、推上额头的面罩，小锤一线白蓝火。

name: 缝衣裳的姑娘
src: 月银纪史诗/第七歌_焚原断刃.md:1317
who: A human tailor's daughter of the grain plains, nineteen, a refugee who fled the burning city through the water channels with nothing but gold thread and needles: about 158 cm, slender and quick-handed. Light auburn hair tied back in a low knot with a strand of gold thread wound through it. Hazel-green eyes that look at clothes before faces. Faint needle-prick marks on her fingertips and a worn bronze thimble on her right middle finger (on the viewer's left when she faces us). Quiet, quick and soft-voiced; everything she owns is patched with bright scraps, and she has never stitched a wheat ear on her own clothes.
build: 158 cm, slender: narrow shoulders, a B-cup, a slim waist.
palette: undyed linen with madder rose, woad blue and weld yellow patches, ash grey, gold thread
casual: A refugee's clothes kept alive by mending: an undyed linen dress to the ankle, straight-cut with long laced sleeves, covered in neat patches of many bright colours, a grey wool shawl tied across the chest, a cloth apron with deep pockets, worn leather shoes; a sewing roll of bone needles and small shears tied at the waist. She holds a spool of gold thread in one hand and a threaded bone needle in the other, the head tilted toward someone's torn sleeve.
private: In the refugee camp at night: a long-sleeved soft wool dress in faded rose, a patched shawl around the shoulders, the hair down over one shoulder, wool stockings and shoes; a half-mended coat over one arm and the bone needle in the other hand, a small, tired smile.
battle: On the road north with the refugees: the patched linen dress under a hooded grey wool travelling cloak whose inner hem is stitched with a line of gold thread that catches the light by itself like a small ward, cloth gaiters over the shoes, a bundle of mended clothes tied on her back, the sewing roll strapped at the waist. She carries no weapon: the gold-thread spool held close in one hand and the bone needle ready in the other, a firm, quiet look.
battle_pose: 3) the road outfit: braced and quiet, the shoulders set, holding the gold-thread spool close to the chest in one hand and a threaded bone needle in the other; she never fights and holds no weapon.
formal: On the night before the climb, finishing a gift: a clean woad-blue linen dress with long sleeves, an undyed linen vest edged with a thin band of gold thread at the collar and no wheat ear on it, a fresh white kerchief over the knot of hair, polished old shoes. Over her forearm she holds a new grey shirt turned to show its back, a single gold-thread wheat ear stitched between the shoulder blades.
art: A close portrait by firelight, her head bent over her sewing and the eyes just lifted to the viewer, soft and unsmiling. Warm fire glow from below, cool ash-grey dusk from behind. Foreground blur: a gold thread drawn through the air and a needle catching the light.
gear: 无位阶（不到启源）｜贫｜不打仗｜不分档｜不到启源的逃难裁缝，不穿甲，第三格画逃难路上那一身，斗篷里缝的金线自己亮一点，是这一段金线织成护符的小魔法。

name: 田埂上拾穗的姑娘
src: 月银纪史诗/第七歌_焚原断刃.md:1223
who: A barefoot gleaner who appears on the field ridges wherever the farm boy goes; she is the harvest goddess walking the world, though no one can prove it. She looks like a grown young woman of about eighteen, small and light, about 152 cm. Pale wheat-gold hair in two loose braids with ripe wheat ears stuck through them, a scatter of freckles across the nose, warm leaf-green eyes with a teasing smile in them that is somehow much older than her face. Bare feet dusty from the field. Her apron always holds just enough gleaned ears to grind one loaf; a small sickle hangs at her apron string and is never used. Playful, curious and light; she listens hardest when others sing the harvest song.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about eighteen, NOT a child: round soft cheeks, freckles across the nose, warm leaf-green eyes, a closed-mouth teasing smile, the gaze calm and very old. Skin shadows a warm pink-orange.
build: 152 cm, small and slight: narrow shoulders, a small A-cup, a slim waist.
palette: pale wheat gold, field green, undyed linen, earth brown, a little poppy red
casual: Gleaning on the field ridge: a straight-cut undyed linen dress to the shin over a long-sleeved shift, a broad sun-faded green apron gathered up in front and holding a bundle of gleaned wheat ears, a cord at the waist with a small sickle hanging from it, bare feet. She holds the apron up in both hands, head tilted, a teasing smile.
private: At dusk while others sing: a long-sleeved faded green wool dress, a straw-coloured shawl, the braids undone into wavy pale gold hair with a few ears still caught in it, bare feet; she twirls a single wheat ear in her fingers, listening hard, the lips moving along with the song.
battle: At the edge of the burnt red earth in the famine winter: the same undyed linen dress and green apron, but the apron hangs empty; a worn grey wool shawl over the shoulders against the wind, bare feet. The small sickle hangs at the cord untouched, and a faint warm green-gold glow lingers along the apron hem like the last warmth of a field. She stands still, both hands open and empty at her sides, the smile gone.
battle_pose: 3) the winter outfit: standing still and quiet, the empty apron hanging, both hands open and empty at her sides, the smile gone, the eyes steady; she never fights and holds no weapon.
formal: At the harvest feast: a clean long-sleeved undyed linen dress with a band of green and gold wheat ears embroidered at the hem, a wreath of ripe wheat ears and red poppies on the braided hair, a fresh green apron full of ears, bare feet. Hands clasped in front, a small attentive smile.
art: A close portrait in low golden evening light from behind, the field glowing: she peeks at the viewer over a raised armful of gleaned wheat, a teasing closed-mouth smile and old, calm eyes. Foreground blur: wheat ears and drifting chaff.
gear: 神（人间扮相，不出手）｜——｜不打仗｜不分档｜祂在人间不动手，第三格画红土线外那一回，围裙是空的，只在围裙边留一点暖光当兆头。

name: 没有羊的老牧人
src: 月银纪史诗/第七歌_焚原断刃.md:1238
who: An old shepherd with no sheep, met every few years on the highland passes and never any older; he is the god of earth wandering the hills, though no one says so. He looks about seventy: very tall and big-boned, about 200 cm, heavy-shouldered and a little stooped, standing as still as a rock. Long iron-grey hair and a long iron-grey beard with a faint dark blue sheen, warm red-iron eyes under heavy brows, a face like weathered stone. Huge, gnarled hands. A wool cloak faded to no colour at all and a smooth-worn shepherd's staff whose top has turned the colour of stone. Slow, silent, patient; asked where his sheep are, he says ahead.
face: FACE, as in the references, but old: a weathered man of about seventy with a face like carved stone, deep lines at the eyes and brow, heavy iron-grey eyebrows, warm red-iron eyes, a long iron-grey beard. Skin shadows a warm tone.
build: 200 cm, very tall and big-boned: broad heavy shoulders, a deep chest, long strong arms, slightly stooped.
palette: colourless faded wool, stone grey, iron grey with a dark blue sheen, moss green, worn wood brown
casual: On the hill path: a big hooded cloak of sheep's wool faded to no colour at all, fastened at the throat with a plain bone pin, over a long undyed wool tunic belted with a rope, wool leggings wrapped with thongs, old hide boots; a small cloth bundle of food at the rope belt. He leans on the tall smooth-worn shepherd's staff, its top turned stone-coloured, standing perfectly still, the eyes on the stones at his feet.
private: Eating what someone gave him: the cloak pushed back off the shoulders, the long wool tunic with the sleeves pushed up off huge forearms, a heel of bread in one hand and a wooden cup of water in the other, the staff leaning against his shoulder. Slow and unhurried, a faint kind look.
battle: Crossing the high pass in winter: the colourless wool cloak drawn close with the hood up, snow caught in the grey beard, the rope belt, wrapped leggings and hide boots; he carries no weapon. He grips the stone-topped staff planted upright before him, and a faint warm brown-gold light runs in thin veins down the staff like ore in rock.
battle_pose: 3) the winter outfit: standing still against the wind, the hood up, both huge hands resting on the planted staff, the eyes calm and steady; he never fights and holds no weapon.
formal: As the highlanders would dress him for a shepherds' feast: a clean undyed wool cloak with a broad border of moss-green weave, pinned with a large round brooch of plain grey stone, a long wool tunic and a wide leather belt, the beard combed; the staff held upright in one hand. Standing straight, the shoulders square as a wall, a small calm smile.
art: A portrait of him sitting on a boulder high on a grass slope, as still as the stone, gazing at the viewer with calm red-iron eyes, the staff across his knees. Cool mountain light from one side, warm late sun on the other. Foreground blur: highland grass and a trickle of spring water over stones.
gear: 神（人间扮相，不出手）｜——｜不打仗｜不分档｜祂在人间不动手，第三格画大雪埋山口那一夜，杖身里一线矿脉似的暖光是兆头，不拿兵器。
